market.domesticSlice: figures are India-specific; this is a domestic policy-driven build-out story (PLI, ALMM), not primarily an export market

structureFacts: ALMM (Approved List of Models and Manufacturers), enforced by MNRE, is legally required for government-funded solar projects — a hard regulatory gate, not a nice-to-have certification.

From June 2026, module manufacturers on ALMM List-I will be required to buy cells only from List-II manufacturers for modules installed in India — a structural rule that rewards vertically-integrated module+cell manufacturers.

The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme supports 48.3 GW of solar cell manufacturing capacity expansion, of which ~36.5% has already been established — real, large-scale policy support driving the build-out.

REAL RISK, not just upside: Wood Mackenzie flags India's solar manufacturing capacity set to exceed 125 GW, creating an overcapacity challenge with inventory reaching 29 GW — the sector is not simply short of supply; new entrants are scaling into a market with a real glut risk.

adoptionStructure.note: Demand is driven by government tender cycles and private EPC contracting, gated by ALMM qualification — not a consumer replacement-rate market.

drivers: ALMM qualification is the hard gate for government-funded projects — the single most important credential in this segment.
From June 2026, module-cell vertical integration becomes structurally rewarded (List-I makers must source cells from List-II).
Price and delivery reliability against a large order-book/tender pipeline, same as any large-scale industrial supplier.
